main_notes.title: Everyday devices connected to the internet
Devices can make or receive VoIP calls
Example: Your smart fridge calling you when out of milk
Integration of multiple devices for communication purposes

key_terms.definition: A fifth-generation cellular network technology that offers significantly faster data transfer rates, lower latency, and higher capacity compared to previous generations.

A system of interconnected physical devices, vehicles, home appliances, and other items embedded with sensors, software, and connectivity which enable these objects to collect and exchange data over the internet.

examples: Your smart fridge calling you when it detects that you are running low on milk.
A smart speaker automatically scheduling a video call for your next meeting based on your calendar entries.
Wearable devices like fitness trackers sending real-time health updates to your smartphone or other connected devices.
connections: 5G and IoT together enhance the capabilities of smart devices by providing faster data transfer rates, enabling more efficient communication between devices.
VoIP integration in smart devices allows for seamless voice communication across a wide range of devices, from smartphones to home appliances.
Smart homes and offices benefit from automated scheduling and reminders, improving productivity and convenience.
questions: How does 5G improve the quality of VoIP calls compared to previous generations?
What are some potential applications of IoT in smart homes and offices beyond just making or receiving VoIP calls?
